clue.text: Knockabout comedians have a drink with the O'Grady girl

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl
and means with, joining two things
Judy O'Grady, from Kipling's line 'the Colonel's Lady an' Judy O'Grady'

explanation.surface: A pair of slapstick comics share a drink with a girl called O'Grady.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Ladies' ends 'the Colonel's Lady an' Judy O'Grady are sisters under their skins'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional British seaside puppet show stars a quarrelsome pair whose violent slapstick is the whole act.

clue.text: Cancel detailed arrangement in part when doing wrong

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for part
arrangement says the letters are rearranged
detailed means the word has its tail, the final letter, cut off

explanation.surface: A planned arrangement is partly cancelled when it goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts CANCEL to CANCE; 'arrangement' rearranges it to ECCAN; 'in' sets that inside PT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sinning or offending, from the Latin for committing a fault.

clue.text: Clementine's shoe number's the sartorial limit

explanation.surface: Clementine's shoe size is as far as smart dressing can go.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' her shoes were 'number nine'; dressed 'to the nines' is dressed perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The song gives Clementine size-nine shoes, and dressing to the nines means as smart as can be.

clue.text: Sounds healthy if overweight — a bit cold in the fall

definitions.text: a bit cold in the fall

indicators.note: sounds says the word for healthy is said out loud to give a different spelling

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
read as over weight: a stone, the British unit of 14 pounds, placed below

explanation.surface: Someone sounds healthy despite being overweight and having a slight cold in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is 14 lb, the British unit for body weight; in this down clue the first piece sits over it. 'Fall' is falling from the sky, not autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice dropping from the clouds is a small piece of frozen weather.

clue.text: Absence of approval for the recess

parts.note: no means none, an absence
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Approval is not given for the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' is a small corner, not a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sheltered corner set into a room is an alcove.

clue.text: All should be ready to attend this rally

definitions.text: All should be ready to attend this rally

parts.words: All should be ready to attend this rally
parts.note: a large gathering of Scouts, whose motto is 'Be prepared', so all are ready

explanation.walkthrough: The Scout motto is 'Be prepared'.
explanation.definitionFit: A big Scout gathering, or any lively celebration, is the rally meant.

clue.text: Charge for turning over the garden with it

indicators.note: turning over means the word for garden is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot for flowers

explanation.surface: A fee for digging over the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses BED to DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum entered against an account is a charge made to it.

clue.text: Such precautions needed if a false mistake is made

definitions.text: Such precautions needed if a false mistake is made

indicators.note: a mistake is made with the letters, so they are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Safeguards are needed in case an error is committed.
explanation.walkthrough: IF A FALSE rearranged gives the answer, and the whole clue describes such measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A system built to stay safe when a component goes wrong has protective backup measures.

clue.text: Recompense for one making out his cheque the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the drawer of a cheque is the person who writes it

explanation.surface: Someone is repaid for writing out his cheque incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment given in return for service is a recompense.

clue.text: Possibly cue in class of Babylonian characters

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the following words are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: a form is a class or year group in a British school

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether to bring in a class studying ancient Babylonian script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges CUE IN into CUNEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedge-shaped script pressed into clay tablets was the writing system of Babylon and its neighbours.

clue.text: Follower of a track event, a bit boring with this

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter after A is B
a race is an athletics event run on a track

explanation.surface: A spectator who follows athletics finds part of a race tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' is not dull here: a drill bit is held in a hand tool for boring holes, the bit and its holder.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpenter's hand drill is called a bit and its cranked holder, used together for drilling holes.

clue.text: Beast of burden is one found in Umbria

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a classic pack animal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pack animal is the kind of thing you meet in the Italian countryside of Umbria.
explanation.walkthrough: The town of St Francis sits in Umbria, central Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill town of St Francis is in the central Italian region, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Maize cake's the wrong one everybody rejected

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rejected means the word for everybody is sent back, so read backwards

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A maize pancake is condemned as the wrong one by everyone who tastes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican flatbread is made from maize flour, a thin unleavened round.

clue.text: Turning to description of dry wine for fish

indicators.note: turning means the letters of both pieces that follow are read backwards together

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone turns to describing a dry wine to go with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses TO BRUT as a whole run, giving the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The flatfish is a prized European sea fish with firm white flesh.

clue.text: Gunners training as para troopers show some precipitation

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
paratroopers train for the drop, so the gunners are in drop training

explanation.surface: Artillerymen training as paratroops put on a show in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: RA are the Royal Artillery; paratroops being 'in drop' training gives the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling bead of water is a small part of a shower.

clue.text: Locker and table, typist for the use of

parts.note: a key is what locks a door, so a locker
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A list of office furniture: a locker and a table for the typist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locker' looks like a cupboard but is the thing that locks.
explanation.definitionFit: The bank of lettered keys is what a typist strikes to put words on paper.

clue.text: Missile making a loud noise on the new range

parts.note: a boom is a loud deep noise

indicators.note: new says the letters of the next word are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A rocket makes a loud bang at the new firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RANGE into ERANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Aboriginal throwing stick is a weapon hurled through the air.

clue.text: French native in the town of Titipu perhaps

definitions.text: in the town of Titipu perhaps

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is found in a Japanese town.
explanation.walkthrough: Titipu is the town of Gilbert and Sullivan's 'The Mikado'; a performer in those operas, first staged at the Savoy Theatre, has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Savoy in France, and a Gilbert and Sullivan performer from the Savoy Theatre company.

clue.text: Pearl 1,006? That's uncommonly old!

indicators.note: uncommonly says the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1,000 and VI is 6

explanation.surface: A pearl valued at 1,006 must be remarkably ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: PEARL plus MVI, rearranged because of 'uncommonly', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the earliest ages of the world is extremely ancient.

clue.text: Earth for instance or what grows out of earth initially

indicators.note: out of puts the growing thing outside the next letter, which it emerges from

parts.note: a plant is a thing that grows

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Earth, or something that sprouts from the soil at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' places PLANT around E, the first letter of 'earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Our world is one of the bodies circling the sun.

clue.text: Game little girl associated with a crook

definitions.text: little girl associated with a crook

explanation.surface: A plucky little girl links up with a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is the hiding game played with babies; the nursery rhyme shepherdess carried a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The peekaboo game shares its name with the nursery rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep and carried a crook.

clue.text: A coat for an anaemic little child

parts.note: an anaemic person looks pale
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A coat bought for a sickly toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose outer overcoat is the garment named.

clue.text: Some said to result from something more

explanation.surface: A remark that some people make about getting more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some said' is SUM: a sum is the result of this operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is what you get by totting numbers up; also an extra item added on.

clue.text: Not all quite heedless of the sound of Minnehaha?

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone not entirely careless of the sound of Longfellow's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Minnehaha in Longfellow's 'Hiawatha' means 'laughing water', so her sound is a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnehaha's name means laughing water, and the answer is a giggle.

clue.text: Family quarrel with a student of old system of government

parts.note: a feud is a long quarrel between families
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A family row involves a student of an old political order.
explanation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval system of lords and vassals holding land for service is the old order meant.

clue.text: Travel this way to the house

explanation.surface: Directions for travelling to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is going by car; the other is the private road up to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: You go by car this way, and a private approach road leads to a house.

clue.text: Fingal's dog found in a tub

explanation.surface: The hero Fingal's hound turns up in a tub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ossian's legends Fingal's hound is Bran; a bran tub is a British fair's lucky dip, prizes buried in cereal husks.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Irish hero's hound bore this name, and cereal husks fill the lucky-dip tub at a fete.

clue.text: Arden's subject of an early translation

explanation.surface: A writer named Arden chose a subject for an early translated work.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem is 'Enoch Arden'; the Bible's patriarch was 'translated' to heaven without dying (Hebrews 11:5).
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's sailor is named Arden, and the Genesis patriarch was taken bodily to heaven, an old sense of translate.

clue.text: It is a real disaster if he misses the trapeze

definitions.text: It is a real disaster if he misses the trapeze

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A circus act goes badly wrong if the performer misses the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: IT IS A REAL rearranged gives the performer; the whole clue describes his fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze artist or high-wire performer works in the air above the ring.

clue.text: One of three beating his breast on hearing the loud bassoon

definitions.text: One of three beating his breast on hearing the loud bassoon

parts.words: One of three beating his breast on hearing the loud bassoon
parts.note: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner stops one of three men going to a feast, who beats his breast when he hears the loud bassoon

explanation.walkthrough: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner opens with the Mariner stopping 'one of three' on the way to a marriage feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's listener is an invitee to a marriage feast, detained by the Mariner's tale.
